name: PADAM NOCTURNE
description: Local memory for AI agents in one SQLite file on the user's machine: masks secrets, holds injected orders for the owner and fences search results as data. Search, history and stats keep Guard's usual handling; every tool that changes memory or exports all of it is gated on review. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Tools read and write only the local SQLite file. Memory text leaves the machine only if OLLAMA_URL is set to another host (default: localhost) for embeddings; the optional [embed] model is fetched once from Hugging Face and gets no memory.
No erase tool over MCP: forgetting, Arweave anchoring and inheritance are owner-only CLI commands (padam forget, l3, legacy, panic).
padam_write stays on review: command recognition is a help, not the wall, and injected commands can still pass it. Sealed Red Team results with every failure: docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md.

PADAM holds command-like text and identity changes for the owner (padam review); outside text is held only when the agent labels it external, which PADAM cannot verify. PADAM_STRICT=1 holds every agent write.
Secret-looking values are masked before storing; recalled memory is fenced as data with a fresh 128-bit marker that stored text cannot predict (docs/FENCING_SPEC.md).
padam_export returns active and, by default, superseded records as JSON, so it stays on review; padam_search returns only matching records, fenced.
This entry matches uvx padam-nocturne. Other launches (pip install, python -m padam.mcp_server, a git checkout) keep Guard's normal handling.
Give each project its own memory file with PADAM_DB; run padam_sleep with dry_run first to see what a cycle would change.
